title.narrative: Improved implementation of Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work through protection of workers from unacceptable forms of work

description.narrative: The Country Programme Outcome will continue to promote the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, adopted in 1998 and amended in 2022, is an expression of commitment by governments, employers' and workers' organizations to uphold basic human values - values that are vital to our social and economic lives. It affirms the obligations and commitments that are inherent in membership of the ILO, namely: freedom of association and the effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining, the elimination of all forms of forced or compulsory labour the effective abolition of child labour, the elimination of discrimination in respect of employment and occupation and a safe and healthy working environment. The nature and scope of the problem is reflected at the national level in the Republic of Mozambique. Among the Children in paid employment, the sectors Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing while the mining and quarrying also have incidences of child labour. Nevertheless, the number of children engaging in mining activities has also increased markedly in recent years. The high level of informality in the especially in areas where workers in the construction sector are found due to demand for increased infrastructure and where monitoring or inspections by labour officers, law enforcement, or social services agencies is limited, also contributes to the presence of child labour including other decent work deficits such as lack of safety standards for workers, lack of representation of workers, no contracts, high informality and poor sanitation of the work place. The intervention will be implemented in collaboration with UNESCO (UNRPRD project), Associations of People with Disabilities (ADEMO) and the Forum of People with Disabilities and the TVET institution (IFEPELAC), Ministry of Health, National AIDS Council, Star Initiative, UNAIDS, UNDP and UN Women in rolling out VCT@WORK interventions.
